daily_summary: Today's top-scoring papers represent significant advancements in the field of AI, with a particular emphasis on multimodal learning, efficient scaling, and real-time synthesis. Notably, the Intern-S1-Pro paper presents a trillion-scale scientific multimodal foundation model, while MSA: Memory Sparse Attention and LagerNVS: Latent Geometry for Fully Neural Real-time Novel View Synthesis offer innovative solutions for efficient end-to-end memory model scaling and real-time novel view synthesis, respectively. Meanwhile, papers like Vega: Learning to Drive with Natural Language Instructions and OmniWeaving: Towards Unified Video Generation with Free-form Composition and Reasoning push the boundaries of AI's ability to interact with and generate complex, dynamic environments.

hot_topics.insight: Research is advancing in multimodal foundation models, with papers like Intern-S1-Pro and LagerNVS showcasing trillion-scale models and latent geometry for novel view synthesis.
Efficient attention mechanisms are being explored, as seen in MSA: Memory Sparse Attention, which enables end-to-end memory model scaling to 100M tokens.
AVO: Agentic Variation Operators is introducing new methods for autonomous evolutionary search, which could lead to breakthroughs in optimization and exploration.

key_developments: Intern-S1-Pro achieves a trillion-scale scientific multimodal foundation model, setting a new benchmark for large-scale models.
MSA: Memory Sparse Attention enables efficient end-to-end memory model scaling, which could lead to significant performance improvements in various AI applications.
Vega: Learning to Drive with Natural Language Instructions demonstrates the potential of natural language instructions for controlling complex systems like autonomous vehicles.
